claims.claim: Firefly links launch, lunar landing, orbital vehicles and autonomy/software around a shared mission stack; common flight technologies and co-located manufacturing can create cross-program learning and production leverage if reliability scales.

The key causal bottleneck is repeatable mission execution: demand and contracted missions create value only if launch cadence, spacecraft production and regulatory access convert backlog into successful missions.

risks.risk: Successor bottlenecks include launch-site/regulatory availability, engine/vehicle production and simultaneous execution across multiple programs.

unknowns.unknown: Block II's sustainable flight rate is not yet demonstrated in service.

claims.claim: Record revenue and contract momentum do not yet establish self-funding economics: Q2 net loss was $92.3M, first-half net loss $189.0M, and first-half operating cash flow remained negative while the company raised $181.6M net in a common-stock offering.

Execution risk is explicit rather than hypothetical: Firefly's 10-Q identifies inability to operate Alpha at anticipated launch rates, Eclipse development/delivery, major-customer/vendor dependence and government funding/regulatory changes as material risks.

risks.risk: Equity financing demonstrates available capital but also creates dilution exposure while operating cash flow remains negative.
Government program concentration exposes schedules and demand to appropriations and regulatory timing.
A launch failure or Eclipse delay can propagate across customer confidence and revenue timing.

contradictions.contradiction: Rapid revenue growth and a broader manifest coexist with continuing losses and an unproven high-cadence launch configuration.
contradictions.disposition: execution tension requiring longitudinal evidence, not present thesis rejection

unknowns.unknown: Backlog conversion margins and long-run free-cash-flow economics remain Alpha-owned underwriting gaps.
